例句

  • She felt nervous and anxious before the interview, but she deliberately stayed calm.（面试前她又紧张又焦虑，但她有意让自己保持冷静。）
  • His first business was a failure, but he learned from the experience and later achieved great success.（他第一次创业失败了，但从这段经历里学到了东西，后来取得了很大成功。）
  • Many young people worry about how others will judge them, and this kind of perfectionism can lower their confidence.（很多年轻人担心别人怎么评价自己，这种完美主义会让他们没自信。）
  • The company rejected my application, but I tried to stay positive and not take the criticism personally.（公司拒了我的申请，但我尽量保持乐观，不把批评往心里去。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（最好跟情绪、自信、找工作被拒有关，口语 Part 2 讲经历和写作 Task 2 都常用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Is rejection good for us?（9 月 17 日）。这集讲网上流行的"拒绝疗法"，句子不长，日常口语多，很适合练精听。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：Walt Disney 成功之前，下面哪件事没有发生在他身上？a) he lost his job as an artist b) his first business ran out of money c) his first full length film was a failure
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Hannah 跟陌生人搭话那段语速快、句子短，Claudia Hammond 那段句子长，这两段多听几遍。
  4. 第三遍挑 Hannah 讲自己感受那段（"And actually, walking up to the first person..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：rejection（拒绝）、spike（猛增）、socially anxious（社交焦虑的）、come easier（变得更容易）、perfectionism（完美主义）、appraise（评价，评判）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）

Georgie：Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Georgie.

Neil：And I'm Neil. Don't forget you can find vocabulary, definitions and a worksheet for free on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Georgie：So Neil, today we're talking about rejection. So, rejection means saying no to someone or refusing to accept their idea or suggestion. Neil, how do you feel about rejection?

Neil：Well, nobody likes rejection. But I think as you get older, you get used to it. And probably it's quite a good thing to experience rejection, even if it doesn't feel nice.

Georgie：Yeah, I agree. We can't always get what we want, can we?

Neil：We can't, no. In this podcast, we'll be learning about a new internet trend潮流，趋势 called rejection therapy疗法，治疗 and how people are using it to help them to be more confident. OK. Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie. Lots of famous people have faced rejection in their lives before they became successful, but which of these things did not happen to the animator动画师 Walt Disney before he became successful? Was it:
a) he lost his job as an artist,
b) his first business ran out of money钱用光了, or
c) his first full length film长片，正片 was a failure?

Georgie：I've got no idea, but I'm going to go with选，就选 a) he lost his job as an artist.

Neil：OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.

Georgie：OK Neil. So, most people don't like being rejected, but one thing to try might be something called rejection therapy疗法，治疗. It's a social media trend潮流，趋势 where people record themselves talking to strangers and sometimes being rejected.

Neil：OK. That sounds quite interesting, but let's find out how it works in practice实际上. Hannah Gelbart, host of the BBC World Service podcast What in the World, had a go at试一试 the trend潮流，趋势. Let's see how she got on进展，表现.

Hannah Gelbart：Hey, can I come sit down at your table?

Stranger：Yeah.

Hannah Gelbart：Hey, how's it going?

Stranger：Good, thank you.

Hannah Gelbart：How's your day gone? Good afternoon. How are you doing? Can I drive your cab出租车? Can I? Can I get behind the wheel开车，握方向盘?

Cab出租车 Driver：Don't be silly!

Hannah Gelbart：Don't be silly...! Coming somewhere else to try and face my fears直面恐惧... maybe do a bit of shopping. I was wondering, can I have a nap小睡，打盹 in one of these beds? Can I just try it out试一下? Wow – I didn't expect that one to be a yes!

Georgie：Well, it seems like people were pretty nice to Hannah in those examples.

Neil：Yes. And she talks with psychologist Claudia Hammond about how she felt during the experiment.

Hannah Gelbart：And actually, walking up to the first person, I felt my adrenaline肾上腺素 really, really spiking猛增，急剧上升. I'm not a socially anxious社交焦虑的 person – I think I'm really confident. But that first thing really scared me. And once I'd done one, the second one came easier变得更容易 and the third one came even easier. And you know, by the fourth time I didn't even mind it whether they said yes or no.

Georgie：Hannah says that when she walked up to the first stranger in the video, she felt her adrenaline肾上腺素 spiking猛增，急剧上升. If something spikes猛增，急剧上升, it increases sharply.

Neil：Hannah is not generally a socially anxious社交焦虑的 person. Someone who is socially anxious社交焦虑的 is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.

Georgie：Each time Hannah tried to speak to a new person, she says, it came easier变得更容易. Come easier变得更容易 is an informal way to say something is easier to achieve.

Neil：Now, this social media trend潮流，趋势 is called rejection therapy疗法，治疗, but it's not a proper form of therapy疗法，治疗. It hasn't been tested.

Georgie：And there are some criticisms批评 of the videos because they involve filming your interactions互动，交往 with strangers, which people might not want.

Neil：But people who post the videos say they boost提升，增强 their confidence. So, why do people want to ask for rejection?

Georgie：Psychologist Claudia Hammond has some ideas, which she shared with Hannah on the BBC World Service podcast What in the World.

Claudia Hammond：What we do know is that there is an increase in perfectionism完美主义. People are more worried now, younger people, about how other people are judging them. And so, I wonder whether that might make people more shy of不敢，害怕做 speaking to strangers – worried that the people will, you know, not appraise评价，评判 them in a good way, and so doing something like this to try to counter抵消，应对 that might feel like a positive step to people, that they're trying to do something. Also, they're fun to watch.

Neil：Claudia says there's an increase in perfectionism完美主义 among young people. Perfectionism完美主义 is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.

Georgie：Young people are also worried about how people will appraise评价，评判 them, which means judge them.

Neil：Deliberately故意地，有意地 looking for rejection might be an extreme way to become more confident, but it can lead to surprising discoveries.

Georgie：Yes, and Hannah found that most strangers she spoke to were friendly and happy to help, so she didn't really experience rejection much at all.

Neil：OK. Georgie, I think it's time now for the answer to my quiz question. I asked you which rejection Walt Disney didn't experience before becoming successful?

Georgie：Yes, and I went for a) I don't think he lost his job as an artist.

Neil：Well, actually, the answer was c) his first full length film长片，正片, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, was not a failure. It was a huge success.

Georgie：Wow! That was his first film? That's really impressive令人印象深刻的.

Neil：It is.

Georgie：OK. Let's recap回顾；总结 the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with rejection, which means saying no or refusing an idea or suggestion.

Neil：The verb spike猛增，急剧上升 means increase suddenly.

Georgie：Someone who is socially anxious社交焦虑的 is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.

Neil：If something comes easier, it's easier to achieve.

Georgie：Perfectionism完美主义 is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.

Neil：And if you appraise评价，评判 someone, you judge them.

Georgie：Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：Thank you for joining us and goodbye.

Georgie：Goodbye.

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（拒绝疗法是什么，Hannah 试了以后感觉怎样，心理学家觉得年轻人为什么会这么做），6 个表达都知道意思，Hannah 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. After three job ______s, she finally got an offer.（被拒）
  2. House prices ______d last year and then fell again.（猛增）
  3. He is a bit ______ ______, so he hates big parties.（社交焦虑的）
  4. Driving was hard at first, but it ______ ______ with practice.（变得更容易，用过去式）
  5. Her ______ means she checks every email five times.（完美主义）
  6. The manager will ______ each employee's work at the end of the year.（评价）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，他的第一部长片《白雪公主和七个小矮人》大获成功，Georgie 选 a 猜错了。填空：1. rejection 2. spike 3. socially anxious 4. came easier 5. perfectionism 6. appraise
